label: Precomputed review of the fixed original fictional exhibit. Not live per-visitor verification.
cost_note: Computed from actual returned usage and the official current price card; included solely because the partner category requires actual run cost disclosure.

review.summary: All six claims check out against the supplied fixture, code, and completed outputs, with one caveat: I cannot recompute the SHA-256 of the SVG here, so hash matching is taken from the supplied artifact and noted as needing byte-level verification. Minor hygiene issues exist (assert failure exposes raw errors, filename regex excludes dots/underscores, ingest hashes are unverifiable from supplied data).

checks.claim: The recovered title matches the heading of the original source.
checks.reason: source_markdown contains 'The Marigold Room' as the only '# ' heading; regex recovers exactly that, and completed page.json matches.

checks.claim: The visitor migration preserves the two fictional display names and visit counts in the stated schema.
checks.reason: legacy_visitors {Asha:3, Mira:1} map field-for-field to schema_version 2 records with display_name/visit_count; completed visitors.json matches, no additions or loss.

checks.claim: The restored portrait reference names the packaged original SVG and records its content hash.
checks.reason: asset.json points to marigold-portrait.svg (matching asset_inventory, not broken old-images/portrait.svg) and records sha256 43e7...5e, identical to approved_plan input hash. Byte-verification is delegated to the application's hash check.

checks.claim: The public contract allows only the three approved repair tool IDs; a pure-helper branch alone does not authorize an additional tool.
checks.reason: public_allowed_tools_contract exposes TOOL_IDS=['recover_title','upgrade_ledger','reconnect_asset'] and validateTools enforces exactly these three; public repair code's shared hash/json helpers are pure utilities, and its materializeRepair throws on any other toolId.

checks.claim: Reviewing these pure functions and outputs cannot establish durable Temporal retry behavior or universal exactly-once execution.
checks.reason: Nothing supplied demonstrates durability guarantees; the pure functions are deterministic for finite inputs, but retry/persistence semantics are outside the evidence. DATA_NOTICE also states runs are lost on restart.

checks.claim: This is a precomputed second opinion on a fixed synthetic exhibit, not live per-visitor verification or proof that arbitrary software can be repaired.
checks.reason: Input scope, execution_scope, and authorized_plan restrict review to the packaged fictional exhibit; no live visitor processing is present or verified.

risk: Output hash equality with the ingest-side plan hash is copied text here; only the application's byte-level hash check is authoritative.
Errors surface via node:assert, which exposes internal details to callers; explicit validation would be cleaner.
Filename regex rejects valid basenames (underscores, dots) though fine for this fixture.
No round-trip check that legacy counts are non-negative (Number.isInteger permits negative values).
review.scope: Static review of the supplied fixture, source markdown, SVG text, public repair/contract code, approved plan, and completed local outputs only. No running system, filesystem, network, or hash computation was executed; byte/hash checks by the application remain authoritative. Not a security certification.

scope: Only the packaged fictional source, allowed-tool contract, pure repair code, approved plan and completed local outputs were supplied. No user archive, private plans, secrets, external tools or web search.
authority: A model second opinion. Deterministic input/output byte checks remain authoritative. No generic software repair or exactly-once guarantee.
author_validation_notes: The exact supplied snapshot contains only the three approved repair branches; the allowed-tool contract independently rejects other IDs.
The negative-count observation is a limitation if this helper is generalized. A direct pure-function check permits a negative integer, but the fixed original visitor records have positive counts.
Source and output hashes are computed by the application. This model response did not run a filesystem, Temporal service, worker or hash tool, and cannot establish recovery or exactly-once execution.
The model response is preserved as one precomputed review of its named source/code snapshot. It is not a fresh review of every visitor action or deployment revision.
